title: Chapter 2: Approaches to Ethics
content:
ሰላም የተወደዳችሁ የኢትዮፍሬሽ ተማሪዎች! የEthioFresh Team ለእናንተ አካዳሚያዊ ስኬትና ለፈተና ውጤታማነት የሚተጋው ታማኝ አጋራችሁ፣ ይኸው በብዙዎቻችሁ ጥያቄ መሰረት በMoral and Citizenship Education (Civics) የትምህርት ሞጁል መሠረት የተዘጋጀውን Chapter 2 (Part 1: Approaches to Ethics - ከስሩ እስከ Section 2.3.2.2) በከፍተኛ ደረጃ የተዋቀረ ጥልቅ የቱቶሪያል ኖት ይዞላችሁ ቀርቧል። በዚህ ክፍል ስለ ስነ-ምግባር አቀራረቦች (Approaches to Ethics)፣ Normative Ethics፣ Teleological/Consequentialist Ethics፣ Ethical Egoism እና Psychological Egoism በዝርዝር፣ በምሳሌዎችና በፈተና ማታለያዎች ታጅቦ ተዘጋጅቷል። አብራችሁኝ ቆዩ👇👇👇

2.1. Chapter Introduction

Human beings constantly ask fundamental questions about the nature of morality. In the process of prescriptive inquiry, we employ a specific vocabulary and invoke moral theories to explain the nature of morality. All moral theories essentially address three core questions:

  • What is Good?
  • Why is it Good?
  • Where is the Good located?
If there is anything "easy" about moral inquiry, it is the fact that there are only three basic kinds of prescriptive moral theories: teleological theories, deontological theories, and virtue-based theories. Unfortunately, these theories often (but not always) provide different and mostly conflicting answers to these basic questions. This chapter aims to introduce students to these various ethical theories.

👉 የሰው ልጅ በዕለት ተዕለት ህይወቱ ስለ ሞራልና ስነ-ምግባር ማንነት ጥያቄዎችን ይጠይቃል። የትኛውም የሞራል ቲዎሪ (Moral Theory) የሚያተኩረው በሦስት ዋና ዋና ጥያቄዎች ላይ ነው፦ 1) ጥሩ (Good) የሚባለው ምንድን ነው? 2) ለምን ጥሩ ሆነ? 3) የት ነው የሚገኘው?

👉 በስነ-ምግባር ጥናት ውስጥ ሦስት መሰረታዊ ትእዛዛዊ/ደንብ-ሰጪ የሞራል ቲዎሪዎች (Prescriptive Moral Theories) አሉ፦
1. Teleological Theories (ውጤት ተኮር ቲዎሪዎች)
2. Deontological Theories (ግዴታ/ህግ ተኮር ቲዎሪዎች)
3. Virtue-based Theories (በጎ-ምግባር/ባህሪ ተኮር ቲዎሪዎች)
እነዚህ ቲዎሪዎች ለላይኞቹ ጥያቄዎች የሚሰጡት መልስ የተለያየና አንዳንዴም የሚጋጭ በመሆኑ፣ በዚህ ምዕራፍ እያንዳንዳቸውን በጥልቀት ተንትነን እናያለን።

2.3. Normative Ethics

Normative ethics is the branch of ethics that formulates moral standards and rules to guide human action. We begin our review of problems and views in normative ethics starting with the theory of obligation, moving to the theory of moral value, and finally to the theory of nonmoral value.

The ultimate concern of the normative theory of obligation is to guide us in making decisions and judgments about actions in particular situations. A main concern is to guide us as agents trying to decide what we should do in specific cases. However, we want to know more than just what we ourselves should do; we also wish to make judgments about what others should do, whether what someone did was right or wrong, and so forth. In all these capacities—as agents, spectators, advisers, instructors, judges, and critics—our primary question is: "How may or should we decide or determine what is morally right for a certain agent to do in a certain situation?"

Normative Ethics features:

  • Offers theories or accounts of the best way to live by evaluating actions systematically based on outcomes, duties, or motivations.
  • Includes ethical theories such as utilitarianism, deontology, virtue ethics, principlism, narrative ethics, and feminist ethics.
  • Poses fundamental questions such as: Are there general principles or rules that we could follow which distinguish between right and wrong? or Are there virtues and/or relationships that we can nurture in order to behave well?

👉 Normative Ethics (ደንብ-ሰጪ ስነ-ምግባር) ምንድን ነው?
ደንብ-ሰጪ ስነ-ምግባር በሰዎች የዕለት ተዕለት ድርጊት ላይ መመሪያ የሚሰጡ፣ ትክክለኛና ስህተት የሆኑ ተግባራትን የሚለዩ የመመዘኛ መርሆዎችን (Moral Standards) የሚያጠና የህግ/ደንብ ዘርፍ ነው። ጥናቱን የሚጀምረው ከTheory of Obligation (የግዴታ ቲዎሪ) በመነሳት ወደ Theory of Moral Value እና Theory of Nonmoral Value በመሸጋገር ነው።

👉 እኛ ሰዎች በህይወታችን ድርጊት ፈፃሚዎች (Agents) ብቻ ሳንሆን ታዛቢዎች፣ መካሪዎች፣ ፈራጆችና ተቺዎችም በመሆናችን ዋናው ጥያቄያችን፦ "አንድ ግለሰብ በአንድ የተወሰነ ሁኔታ ውስጥ ምን ማድረግ እንዳለበት እንዴት መወሰን እንችላለን?" የሚለው ነው። Normative Ethics ሰዎች እንዴት መኖር እንዳለባቸው መመሪያ ይሰጣል።

2.3.1. Teleological Ethics (Consequentialist)

Teleological ethics, derived from the Greek word 'Telos' meaning end, goal, or purpose, is also known as Consequentialist Ethics. It operates under the maxim "The end justifies the means." It stresses that the consequences of an action determine its morality or immorality. An action is judged as right or wrong, moral or immoral, depending solely on what happens as a result of it. Even if one has the best intention or follows the highest moral principles, if the resulting outcome of the action is harmful or bad, it must be judged as a morally wrong act.

A teleological theory asserts that the ultimate criterion of what is morally right, wrong, or obligatory is the non-moral value that is brought into being. The final appeal must be to the comparative amount of good produced over evil. Thus, an act is right if and only if it produces, probably produces, or is intended to produce at least as great a balance of good over evil as any available alternative.

It is important to notice that for a teleologist, the moral quality or value of actions, persons, or character traits is dependent on the comparative nonmoral value of what they bring about. To avoid circularity (where moral value depends on moral value), teleologists make moral value dependent on nonmoral good (such as pleasure, happiness, knowledge, power, self-realization). Teleologists hold various views about what constitutes nonmoral good:

  • Hedonists: Identify the good with pleasure and evil with pain (e.g., Epicurus, Jeremy Bentham, John Stuart Mill).
  • Non-Hedonists / Ideal Utilitarians: Identify the good with power, knowledge, self-realization, perfection, etc. (e.g., G.E. Moore, Hastings Rashdall).

Comparison with Deontological Theories:
Deontological theories deny what teleological theories affirm. Deontologists assert that the rightness or wrongness of an action depends on features of the act itself (such as keeping a promise, being just, or obeying God's/state commands) rather than the value of its consequences. For a deontologist, an action can be morally right even if it does not promote the greatest balance of good over evil.

👉 Teleological / Consequentialist Ethics (ውጤት ተኮር ስነ-ምግባር)፦
'Teleological' የሚለው ቃል 'Telos' ከሚለው የግሪክ ቃል የተገኘ ሲሆን ትርጉሙም ግብ፣ መጨረሻ ወይም ውጤት (End/Goal) ማለት ነው። የመጨረሻ መሪ መርሆው "The end justifies the means" (ግብ/ውጤት መንገዱን ያጸድቃል) የሚል ነው። የሁኔታዎች ውጤት ብቻ የአንድን ድርጊት ጥሩነት ወይም መጥፎነት ይወስናል። አንድ ሰው ምንም ያህል ጥሩ his/her ሀሳብ (Intention) ቢኖረው፣ የድርጊቱ ውጤት መጥፎ ከሆነ ድርጊቱ "ስህተት/Immoral" ይባላል።

👉 Nonmoral Good እና Moral Value፦ Teleologistዎች የድርጊትን ጥሩነት የሚለኩት ድርጊቱ በሚያስገኛቸው ሞራላዊ ባልሆኑ ጥቅሞች/እሴቶች (Nonmoral goods) ነው፤ ለምሳሌ ደስታ (Pleasure)፣ እውቀት (Knowledge)፣ ስልጣን (Power)፣ እና ራስን ማበልፀግ (Self-realization)።
• Hedonists (ደስታ ተኮሮች): ጥሩ ነገርን ከደስታ (Pleasure)፣ መጥፎን ደግሞ ከሕመም/ስቃይ (Pain) ጋር ያያይዙታል (ምሳሌ፦ Jeremy Bentham, J.S. Mill)።
• Non-Hedonists / Ideal Utilitarians: ደስታ ብቻ ሳይሆን እውቀት፣ ፍጹምነት እና ስልጣንም ዋና እሴቶች ናቸው ይላሉ (ምሳሌ፦ G.E. Moore)።

👉 Real-world Example: በሆስፒታል ውስጥ አንድ ዶክተር በጣም አደገኛና ተላላፊ በሽታ ያለበትን ታካሚ ለህዝብ ደህንነት ሲል ለይቶ አሳድሮ ማከሙ (Quarantine)፤ የካታስትሮፊ/አደጋ ጊዜ የሃብት ክፍፍል ለብዙኃኑ ጥቅም ሲባል መደረጉ ውጤቱ ብዙ ሰዎችን የሚያድን በመሆኑ በTeleological እይታ ትክክለኛ ድርጊት ይባላል።

2.3.2. Egoism: Ethical and Psychological Egoism

Teleologists differ on the question of whose good one ought to try to promote:

  • Ethical Egoism: Holds that an individual ought always to promote their own greatest good (held by Epicurus, Thomas Hobbes, Friedrich Nietzsche).
  • Ethical Universalism / Utilitarianism: Holds that the ultimate end is the greatest general good for everyone.
  • Group Egoism / Particularistic Consequentialism: Holds that the right act is one that promotes the greatest good for a specific group (e.g., nation, class, family, or race).
  • Pure Ethical Altruism: Contends that the right act is that which most promotes the good of other people.
In common understanding, moral behavior is assumed to have to do with not being overly concerned with oneself, and selfishness is considered unacceptable. However, in Western intellectual history, the view that humans are built to look out for themselves ("looking out for number one") has been defended through Psychological Egoism and Ethical Egoism.

2.3.2.1. Ethical Egoism

Ethical Egoism is a normative theory about how we ought to behave. It implies that we ought to be selfish, or more gently, self-interested. Calling the theory "ethical" does not mean there is a decent way to be selfish; it simply means it advocates egoism as a moral rule.

Core Principle "You Should Look After Yourself":
Ethical egoists insist that if you do not take advantage of a situation, you are foolish. Morality, according to them, is a result of self-interest. They present a slanted version of the Golden Rule ("Do unto others as you would have them do unto you"). An ethical egoist treats others well only because doing so increases the chance of receiving good treatment in return—acting solely for oneself, not for others.

Case Study — The Good Samaritan Example:
Some years ago, a Good Samaritan stopped to help a man whose car had broken down on the freeway. The man shot and killed the Samaritan, stole his car, and led the police on a chase before being killed in a shoot-out. While most people admire the Good Samaritan, an ethical egoist would say that the Samaritan did the wrong thing. For ethical egoism, the only rule is: "Look after yourself; you have no business stopping for anybody on the freeway; if you do, you are throwing your life away."

Historical & Political Context (Machiavelli):
Italian statesman Niccolo Machiavelli (1469–1527) argued that if the end is to maintain political power for oneself, one's king, or one's political party, then this justifies any means required—including force, surveillance, or deceit. While consequentialist, Machiavellianism does not qualify as utilitarianism because it lacks the common good as its ultimate end.

Formal Argument for Ethical Egoism:

  1. We all always seek to maximize our own self-interest (definition of psychological egoism).
  2. If one cannot do an act, one has no obligation to do that act (ought implies can).
  3. Altruistic acts involve putting other people's interests ahead of our own (definition of altruism).
  4. Altruism contradicts psychological egoism and is therefore impossible (by premises 1 and 3).
  5. Therefore, altruistic acts are never morally obligatory (by premises 2 and 4).

Application Steps for Ethical Egoism:

  • List all possible acts.
  • For each act, see how much net good it would do for you.
  • Identify the act that does the most net good for you.

Important Clarifications on Ethical Egoism:

  • It does not just say one's welfare counts; it says only one's own welfare counts, and others' does not, when making moral decisions.
  • It does not forbid helping others or require harming others. Helping others is allowed if helping them ultimately serves one's own self-interest.
  • It does not demand always doing what is immediately pleasurable; it acknowledges that long-term self-interest may require short-term pain or sacrifice (e.g., exercising, healthy diet, refraining from overeating).

👉 Ethical Egoism (ስነ-ምግባራዊ ግላዊነት)፦
Ethical Egoism ደንብ-ሰጪ (Normative) ቲዎሪ ሲሆን፣ ሰዎች እንዴት መኖር እና ማድረግ እንደሚገባቸው (Ought to do) ይናገራል። መርሆውም፦ "እያንዳንዱ ሰው ሁልጊዜ የራሱን ጥቅም ብቻ ማስቀደም አለበት" የሚል ነው።

👉 ምሳሌ (The Good Samaritan Case): አንድ በጎ አድራጊ ሰው በመንገድ ላይ መኪናው የተበላሸበትን ግለሰብ ለመርዳት ሲቆም፣ ተረጂው ገድሎት መኪናውን ሰርቆ አመለጣ። አብዛኛው ሰው በጎ አድራጊውን ሲያደንቅ፣ Ethical Egoistዎች ግን "ትልቅ ስህተት ሰርቷል! ህይወቱን በከንቱ ጣለ፣ የራሱን ደህንነት ብቻ መጠበቅ ነበረበት" ይሉታል።

👉 የEthical Egoism ወሳኝ ማብራሪያዎች፦
1. ሌሎችን መረዳትን አይከለክልም፦ ነገር ግን ሌሎችን የምንረዳው በመጨረሻ ለራሳችን ጥቅም እስከጠቀመ ድረስ ብቻ ነው (ምሳሌ፦ የራሳችንን ልጅ ትምህርት ቤት የምንልከው ስለምንወዳቸውና ደስታ ስለሚሰጠን ነው)።
2. የአጭር ጊዜ ደስታ ብቻ አይደለም፦ ለረጅም ጊዜ ጥቅም ሲባል የአጭር ጊዜ ስቃይን መቀበልን ያካትታል (ምሳሌ፦ ስፖርት መስራት፣ አመጋገብን መጠበቅ)።

👉 Real-world Example: አንድ የንግድ ሰው ለድሆች ምጽዋት የሚሰጠው ለድሆቹ አዝኖ ሳይሆን የድርጅቱን ስም አስጠራርቶ የደንበኞቹን ቁጥር ለመጨመር እና ታክስ ለመቀነስ ከሆነ፣ ይህ ድርጊት በEthical Egoism እይታ ሙሉ በሙሉ ትክክለኛና የራስን ጥቅም ያቀደ ድርጊት ነው።

2.3.2.2. Psychological Egoism

The main argument used as a basis for Ethical Egoism is a psychological one—an argument from human nature called Psychological Egoism. Unlike Ethical Egoism (which is normative), Psychological Egoism is a descriptive theory about human nature. It asserts that human beings are so constituted by nature that everyone always seeks their own advantage, welfare, or pleasure.

Key concepts of Psychological Egoism:

  • In Bishop Butler's terms: "Self-love" is the only basic principle in human nature.
  • In contemporary terms: "Ego-satisfaction" is the final aim of all activity, or the "pleasure principle" is the basic drive in every individual.
  • Argument of "Ought Implies Can": If human nature is naturally self-interested, it is unrealistic to propose that we ought to do anything other than what is for our own greatest good. In a sense, we cannot do anything else except by mistake.

Objections & Criticisms of Psychological Egoism:
Philosophers raise significant objections against psychological egoism:

  1. Philosophical Fallacy: One cannot logically infer an ethical conclusion (how we ought to act) directly from a descriptive psychological premise (how we do act).
  2. Primary Appetites vs. Self-Love: The desire for one's own good presupposes the existence of basic primary desires (such as food, fame, or protection). If we did not have these primary appetites first, we would have no "good" to be concerned about.
  3. Existence of Altruistic Desires: The object of a basic desire is often something outside oneself (e.g., eating food, enjoying the ocean view, or desiring to do the right thing). There are genuine altruistic impulses in human nature.
  4. Confusing the Object of Desire with the Resulting Satisfaction ("Putting the cart before the horse"): When a person performs an altruistic act, they may feel satisfaction. However, psychological egoists confuse the object of the desire with the satisfaction that results from attaining it.
    Example: If Person B fails to take Person A to see the ocean, Person B feels frustrated. B is frustrated not because B failed to satisfy B's own ego, but because B wanted Person A to enjoy the ocean. The egoist mistakenly puts the cart before the horse!

👉 Psychological Egoism (ስነ-ልቦናዊ ግላዊነት)፦
Psychological Egoism ስለ ሰው ልጅ ተፈጥሮ የሚገልፅ ግላጭ/ገለፃ ተኮር (Descriptive Theory) ነው። የሰው ልጅ በተፈጥሮው ሁልጊዜ የራሱን ጥቅም፣ ደስታና እርካታ (Self-interest/Ego-satisfaction) ብቻ እንዲፈልግ ሆኖ የተፈጠረ ነው ይላል። በBishop Butler አባባል የሰው ልጅ ተፈጥሮአዊ መሪ መርሆ "Self-love" (ራስን መውደድ) ነው።

👉 የቀረቡበት ዋና ዋና ትችቶች (Criticisms)፦
1. ጋሪውን ከፈረሱ ፊት ማስቀደም ("Putting the cart before the horse")፦ ሰዎች ለሌሎች በጎ ነገር አድርገው ደስታ ስለተሰማቸው ብቻ ድርጊቱ ለራስ ጥቅም ተደረገ ማለት አይቻልም። ደስታው የተገኘው በጎ ለማድረግ በመፈለጋቸው ነው እንጂ፣ ደስታ ፍለጋ ብለው በጎ አላደረጉም።
2. Altruism (ሰብአዊነት/ለሰው ማሰብ) አለ፦ ሰው ከተፈጥሮው መሰረታዊ ፍላጎቶች ባሻገር ለሌሎች ማሰብና ትክክለኛውን ነገር ማድረግ ይችላል።

👉 Real-world Example: በበጎ አድራጎት ስራ የተሰማራ አንድ የዩኒቨርሲቲ ተማሪ ደም ሲለግስ፣ ደም የለገሰው የሰው ህይወት ለማዳን እንጂ በውስጡ እርካታ ለማግኘት ብሎ አይደለም። እርካታው የደግነቱ ውጤት እንጂ የድርጊቱ ዋና አላማ አይደለም! Psychological Egoistዎች ግን ይህንን ያደናግራሉ።

💡 Exam Hint (Ethical Egoism vs Psychological Egoism):
በፈተና ላይ በሚመጡ ጥያቄዎች ላይ እነዚህን ሁለት ቃላት እንዳታደናግሩ፦
• Ethical Egoism = Normative theory (How we OUGHT to behave / ሰዎች እንዴት ማድረግ እንዳለባቸው የሚያዝዝ)።
• Psychological Egoism = Descriptive theory (How humans ACTUALLY ARE / የሰው ልጅ ተፈጥሮአዊ ባህሪ ምን እንደሚመስል የሚገልጽ)።
• "Ought implies can" የሚለው መርሆ የPsychological argument ለEthical Egoism መደገፊያነት የሚጠቀምበት መሰረታዊ ሀሳብ ነው።
• "Putting the cart before the horse" የሚለው ሀሳብ Psychological Egoism ላይ የቀረበ ትልቅ ትችት (Objection) ነው።
